evidence.source: FINDINGS §30.5 (ngspice op read-out on ace8383c at its own best_params)

evidence.quote: `bias.saturated` calls a device saturated when `|Vds| >= 1.5|Vdsat|`. In weak inversion BSIM4's `Vdsat` **collapses to ~55 mV**, so every one of those negative-overdrive devices passes that test by 5–8×: **`bias.saturated` reports all 25 of these transistors as saturated.**

| weak-inversion (`sub`) devices that `bias.saturated` calls **saturated** | **615 / 621 = 99.0%** |
| `bias.saturated` used as a **weak-vs-strong score**, AUC | **0.552** — chance, *with a full DC solve in hand* |

rule: Classify inversion level from gm/Id (sub ~17-20 V^-1, sat ~10-12 V^-1), never from bias.saturated's |Vds| >= 1.5|Vdsat| predicate.

applicability.applies: Every statement in this program's history of the form 'N of 41 corpus circuits are saturated' -- it means CONDUCTING WITH ADEQUATE VDS HEADROOM, not IN STRONG INVERSION, and must be read that way. Also the argument for a gm/Id reparameterization of the sizing space (15-ENGINEER §1.4 item 6).
applicability.not: Not a bug in bias.py -- the predicate answers the question it was built for (is the device conducting?), where it scores AUC 0.737. Nothing measured under it is wrong; the label is narrower than it reads.
